game: NE @ MIA, 2025-09-14 13:00 ET, outdoor, MIA -1.5, total 43.5

script.base: Short home favorite in a 43.5 game (implied MIA 22.5, NE 21.0), so a one-score outdoor game with no blowout snap cut. NE's week-1 run front (2.48 YPC, 1 run of 10+) plus Austin Jackson out should stop De'Von Achane from repeating 7 carries for 55 (7.9 YPC), and Miami has to throw. NE also throws into a 58% Miami blitz; Drake Maye's week-1 EPA/db was +0.05 vs blitz, so the blitz does not by itself kill the Patriots' pass game.
script.flip1: Miami leads early and lives on Achane. Jaylen Wright (doubtful) sits, carries jump into the teens, one crease repeats the week-1 explosive, the rush under dies, and NE abandons Rhamondre Stevenson (7/15) and TreVeyon Henderson (5/27) while Maye airs it to Kayshon Boutte and Stefon Diggs.
script.flip2: NE's 39% blitz plus Jackson out turns Tua into the week-1 blitz version (-1.21 EPA/db vs blitz, +0.05 vs none). Miami checkdowns and deep shots both die, Tyreek Hill's 86 air yards do not convert, the total sags under 43.5, and any Miami receiving over loses while Achane's rush under still cashes on efficiency.

injury_fallout: MIA: Darren Waller out (hip) but he is absent from the week-1 target list, so Tanner Conner (4 tgt/20 yds) may already be the TE; do not assume a big target dump. Austin Jackson out (toe) is the offensive hit: pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws. Jaylen Wright doubtful (knee) pushes carries toward Achane (7/55) and Ollie Gordon (2/4), not a new featured back. Benito Jones out (DT) softens the interior NE will run at. Storm Duck out, Ethan Bonner doubtful, Ashtyn Davis questionable thin the secondary NE will throw at. NE: Christian Gonzalez out (hamstring) is the coverage loss for Hill/Waddle; Keion White out (illness) and Marte Mapu questionable (neck) weaken the same front the Achane under relies on; Morgan Moses questionable (foot) is a game-time pass-pro flag for Maye. Sources: pack official injury report and week-1 target/rush lines. Final inactives not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack (coverage step limited). Proxy only: MIA blitz 58% with YPA left 9.62 (16 att), middle 8.0 (2), right 9.27 (11); NE blitz 39% with YPA left 8.92 (12), middle 11.88 (8), right 12.31 (13).
matchup.pressure: MIA blitz 58% into a Maye who was slightly better when blitzed (+0.05 EPA/db vs -0.04 not blitzed), so NE's intermediate/short game can live. NE blitz 39% into a Tua who was crushed when blitzed (-1.21 vs +0.05). Jackson out should raise the chance that blitz becomes pressure; White out partly offsets NE's rush. No pressure-rate or time-to-throw numbers saved.
matchup.bleeds: NE run defense did not bleed (2.48 YPC, 1 run of 10+). NE pass defense did: 9 passes of 20+ on 37 attempts, middle and right YPA 11.88 and 12.31. MIA run defense bled explosives (3.90 YPC, 6 runs of 10+) more than explosives in the pass game (4 of 20+ on 30).
matchup.overlap: Miami's top air-yard option is Hill (6 tgt, 40 yds, 86 air), aimed at the unit that just allowed 9 explosives and is now without Gonzalez. That is the pass overlap. The run overlap is the opposite: Achane's 7.9 YPC spike runs into the front that allowed 2.48, with Jackson out. Boutte (8 tgt, 103 yds, 137 air) is NE's deep primary, but 103.5 is a spike price, not a weak-spot price, so no Boutte leg.

form: Only week 1 exists (pack weeks < 2); there is no 3-4 game role trend. Achane 7/55 is efficiency, not volume; Gordon 2/4 and a 1-carry Washington cameo. Hill 40 yards on 86 air is an unfinished deep day, not a proven 40-yard role. Waddle 5/30 on only 21 air already converted. Conner 4/20, Malik Washington 5/20 on 51 air. NE: Stevenson 7/15 (2.1 YPC) was the carry leader and was stuffed; Henderson 5/27 plus 6 targets/24 rec yards (air -19) is the explosive and checkdown back. Boutte 8/103/137 and Hunter Henry 8/66/117 look air-yard inflated; Diggs 7/57/61 was the efficient intermediate; Demario Douglas 7 targets for -2 yards is a fluke negative, and the -1.5 stand-in is not a real market. All stand-in lines equal that one-game median.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because the week-1 front was a one-game mask. White is out, Mapu is limited or out, Wright sits, and Achane gets 14-16 carries with one 25-yard crease and finishes over 55.5 the same way 7 carries became 55 last week. In that same game Hill never needs a second shot and stays under 40.5. The other loss path is the split: Achane is stuffed so the under cashes, but the 39% blitz and Jackson's backup turn Tua into the -1.21 version, Hill's 86 air yards die again, and the over loses. n=1 samples plus stand-in lines mean we may be betting numbers a real book never posted. The Hill counter is as strong as the read, which is why it is a lean; the Achane number still needs both extra volume and another explosive to lose, which is why it stays, flagged.
slip_story: One constrained-Miami story, not a shootout: NE stuffs the run (Achane rushyds under) so Tua has to throw at a secondary missing Gonzalez that just bled explosives (Hill recyds over). Do not add Boutte or Henry overs, a total under, or Stevenson/Henderson rush overs; those need a different script. No TD legs. Pass on Douglas -1.5, Gordon 4.5, and Conner 20.5 as stand-in artifacts or empty Waller sleepers.
